newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Grains futures slide in slow Budapest market.
newsitem.headline: Grains futures slide in slow Budapest market.

text.p: Grain futures continued to drop on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) on Monday, with dealers expecting the slide to accelerate in the next days.
"March milling wheat prices will be released on Tuesday and the maturity could drop 1,000 to 1,500 forints per tonne," said Robert Monostori of Agrimpex.

Under BCE rules, if a maturity drops by the daily allowed maximum of 400 forints on five consecutive days, on the sixth day the limit is removed until the daily drop again becomes smaller than 400 forints.
On Monday milling wheat prices closed at between 27,010 forints for March and 22,210 for December.
Monostori added that the May maturity could also be freed from the 400-forint daily limit as it is dragged down by March.
Although market players were aware of excess maize and wheat stocks, recent newspaper reports confirming the surplus accelerated the downward movement, Monostori added.
Maize prices dropped by 100 to 400 forints with nly the March, May and July maturities were traded.
March maize finished at 17,800 forints, down 400, and December also lost 400 to end at 19,400 forints.
Total turnover was a meagre 1,488 contracts or 576.47 million forints, of which maize accounted for 778 contracts and milling wheat for 596.
Lot size is 20,000 kgs for all contracts.
